title: New Acquisition: Kerry James Marshall - Rythm Mastr: This Is How It Begins
excerpt: Hudson Street Library proudly announces the acquisition of Kerry James Marshall's groundbreaking comic series, a powerful blend of Afrofuturism, superhero mythology, and Black cultural history.
content: We are thrilled to announce the acquisition of 'Rythm Mastr: This Is How It Begins' by Kerry James Marshall, edited by Michele Robecchi (Rizzoli Electa, 2025). This comprehensive volume presents Marshall's iconic comic series created in the late 1990s as a direct response to the absence of authentic Black characters and authors in mainstream comics. The series follows Rythm Mastr and his young protégé Farell, superheroes whose powers derive from the seven gods of the Yoruba pantheon. Marshall's characters engage in sophisticated debates about history, philosophy, and politics in vernacular Black English, creating an empowering blend of science fiction and Afrofuturism. Initially serialized in a daily newspaper and presented as a Carnegie International installation, the work has appeared in various forms including light boxes, paintings, graphic prints, and drawings over the past two decades. This first edition hardcover represents the most comprehensive documentation of the character, its genesis, and evolution. As one of America's greatest living painters and chroniclers of the African American experience, Marshall's work continues to challenge and expand our understanding of representation in visual culture. This important addition strengthens our collection of contemporary art, African American art, and graphic narratives, now available for viewing by appointment.

title: New Acquisition: Vince Aletti - Physique: A Photographic History of the Magazine
excerpt: Hudson Street Library has acquired Vince Aletti's seminal work on the influential gay physique magazine that shaped both fitness culture and male imagery from 1951-1990.
content: We're pleased to announce the acquisition of 'Physique: A Photographic History of the Magazine' by Vince Aletti (Process, 2014). This comprehensive study documents the groundbreaking publication that featured pioneering photographers like Bob Mizer, Bruce of Los Angeles, and Lon of New York. Physique magazine operated under the guise of fitness and health but became a crucial platform for gay male imagery during a time of intense censorship. Aletti's book includes rare photographs, magazine covers, and behind-the-scenes documentation that reveals the magazine's profound influence on both fitness culture and LGBTQ+ visual history. This important addition joins our growing collection of LGBTQ+ photography and cultural history materials, now available for viewing by appointment.
